scope: THE DESIGN'S DIFFERENTIATOR MEASURED: the CYCLES. The 23-bond graph carries 4 independent cycles (law doc section 1.2) and FK-trees cannot span cycles (section 1.3a; candidate C2's failure (b)) - the joints-are-materials design should articulate a cycle natively: pose ONE member of a tarsal 3-cycle through its range and the OTHER bonds carry the motion with their rest lengths and pivots UNCHANGED. This lane derives the tarsal pivots with the P6 lane's registered machinery class-adapted, runs the corrected predicate P6' v2 as a per-bond two-arm contrast on all six cycle bonds, and runs the loop-closure demo on both committed tarsal 3-cycles (06-20-25, 07-21-24). Read-only on the kernel, the engine, and the skeleton definition; the lane's writes are its own directory only.

rule_0.statement: THE CLASS-HONEST PIVOT FORM IS OPEN AND IS STATED OPEN. The law's pivot prescription (law doc section 3: 'pivot_mm ... DERIVED from geometry already committed - for the hip, the femoral-head center fit') is written for ONE class only; for gliding/condyled/hinge classes the law prescribes NO pivot form, and for the tarsal 3-cycles' syndesmosis-class pairs section 3(4) prescribes NO DOF at all. verdicts.the_class_verdict: THE CLASS GAP IS REAL AND NOW CARRIES ITS MEASUREMENT. The committed tarsal bonds carry NO class record (no anatomical_reading, no joint_class - only the hips carry one); the design's own section 3(4) classes the 3-cycles' syndesmosis pairs as fusion (NO DOF); the held OpenSim records model the tarsal complex as 1-DOF revolute PinJoints (Rajagopal2016: ankle [-0.6981, +0.5236], subtalar [-0.3491, +0.3491]) and contain NO tibiofibular joint at all - hinge-class DOF for the tibio-foot complex, NO DOF for the syndesmosis pair. THE LAW PRESCRIBES NO PIVOT FORM FOR ANY NON-HIP CLASS - not a hinge axis, not a contact-normal frame, nothing; that prescription gap is THE DESIGN'S NEXT AMENDMENT and is recorded here regardless of outcome. What this lane ADDS to the amendment: the transplanted sphere form is now MEASURED ADMISSIBLE EVIDENCE on the tarsal class - it converges on all six bonds (fixed points, radii 1.80-2.73 mm, RMS at the isosurface's own half-step), it seats the real geometry through the cited subtalar band, and it DISCRIMINATES real from null on all six bonds - while the geometry alone never binds a DOF: the syndesmosis pair (06_20 / 07_21) discriminates too, yet the class record (section 3(4) and both held models) prescribes NO DOF for it. The class record, not the geometry, is what binds DOFs - which is exactly the joints-are-materials frame.
verdicts.the_design_on_cycles: PROVEN AT THE REGISTERED BAND ON THIS CLASS. The design's differentiator - cycles articulate natively under bonds-as-materials - is measured on both committed tarsal 3-cycles: pose the foot member through the cited subtalar range about the driver bond's derived pivot and the loop bond's seats hold (max 2.642331743574 / 2.959470853325 mm <= 3.0) with its pivot UNCHANGED from rest and the side bond's gap EXACTLY constant, at every one of the 11 poses; the FK representation cannot carry the loop bond at ANY pose (3 edges vs tree capacity 2; cyclomatic 4). The demo's own teeth: the null motion breaks the loop (driver displacement breached at every non-rest pose) while its seats stay blind - the same two-leg structure that discriminates the hips. Honest margins: cycle B's loop-seat margin is 0.040529146675 mm (1.35% of the cut) - thin, recorded thin; the successor class amendment (a hinge-axis or contact-frame pivot form prescribed per class) is the lawful way to widen it.
